summary: Recommends that RFC 1643 be reclassified as an Historic document, and gives the reasons supporting that recommendation. It is an informational applicability statement and does not define new technology.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1643 defined management information for half-duplex 10 Mb/s Ethernet. Later Ethernet speeds and full-duplex operation led to newer specifications, so this memo recommends retiring RFC 1643 to Historic status.

questions: what is the ethernet-like interface mib
why was rfc 1643 moved to historic
subtitle: Why RFC 1643's Ethernet interface MIB should be reclassified as Historic.

tldr.problem: RFC 1643 described managed objects only for half-duplex 10 Mb/s Ethernet, while later Ethernet technologies and updated specifications had appeared.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3638 recommends Historic status for RFC 1643 and explains that no standards-track RFC depends on it normatively.
tldr.outcome: The memo points new implementations to RFC 3635 and RFC 2666 instead of RFC 1643.

today: RFC 3638 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1643 by recommending Historic status. It points to RFC 3635 and RFC 2666 for newer specifications.

sections.title: Why the Ethernet MIB Became Outdated
sections.content:
RFC 1643 and its SMIv2 equivalent, RFC 1650, define managed objects for Ethernet-like interfaces. They apply only to half-duplex 10 Mb/s Ethernet.

After their publication, 100 Mb/s, 1000 Mb/s, and 10 Gb/s Ethernet were developed, and full-duplex operation at 10 Mb/s was standardized. Updates to RFC 1650 added objects for newer technologies and deprecated some objects.
sections.plainLanguage: The old MIB covered one specific Ethernet type. Faster Ethernet and full-duplex operation led to newer management specifications.

sections.title: The Recommendation
sections.content:
The memo calls RFC 1643 obsolete and recommends that it be reclassified as Historic. It says RFC 1650 had already been officially retired in 1998.

New implementations, including ones that support only half-duplex 10 Mb/s interfaces, should follow the latest specifications named in the memo: RFC 3635 and RFC 2666. The updates also require EtherLike-MIB implementations to support the MAU-MIB.
sections.plainLanguage: Even an implementation for the older Ethernet interface should follow the newer specifications named by the memo. RFC 1643 is recommended for Historic status.

sections.title: Effect on Other Standards
sections.content:
The authors report that no standards-track RFC cites RFC 1643 as a normative reference. They identify five standards-track RFCs that cite it, but describe those citations as non-normative.

Some citations give history or a warning, and one appears only in an ASN.1 comment. The RFC states that reclassification itself has no effect on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors checked other standards and found no normative dependency on RFC 1643. They say moving it to Historic has no security effect by itself.
